title: Applied-Energistics-2 issue #8754: Unexpected item consume when enable the replace mode of crafting partterns
text:
[issue by L2750558108]
### Describe the bug

For two crafting recipes, A and B, where A accepts item types T1 and T2, and recipe B only accepts T2. In a crafting tree where recipes A and B need to be crafted in sequence, the material T2 for recipe B is already prepared before crafting recipe A for some reason (possibly due to leftover materials from preparing other recipes). If the replace material option in recipe A's parttern is enabled, when crafting recipe A, the crafting system may prematurely consume the T2 material that was originally intended for recipe B. By the time you get to craft recipe B, only the T1 material that should have been consumed by recipe A remains, making it impossible to craft recipe B, which causes the craft line to get stuck in the planned craft state.

Specifically, when crafting a 256M quantum crafting storage, there are two recipes in sequence: first craft a 1k item storage compent and then a Fluix crystal (used for 2^3 space components). The recipe for the 1k item storage component accepts both regular and charged certus crystals, while the Fluix crystal only accepts charged ones. When crafting the 1k item storage component, it is possible to accidentally use up the charged certus crystals that were intended for the Fluix crystal(because the not charged certus crytus orginally prepare for the recipe is provided by a ME Level Emitter in the certus crytus farm and need time to get), leading to a craft blockage.

### How to reproduce the bug

1. Prepare a crafting line for 256M quantum crafting storage, the fluix crystals is crafted by Reaction Chamber and the certus crytus is provided by

title: Applied-Energistics-2 issue #8754: Unexpected item consume when enable the replace mode of crafting partterns
text:
to a craft blockage.

### How to reproduce the bug

1. Prepare a crafting line for 256M quantum crafting storage, the fluix crystals is crafted by Reaction Chamber and the certus crytus is provided by a crytus farm
2. Run the craft for 256M quantum crafting storage and wait for the stuck.

### Expected behavior

It should not be stuck

### Additional details

_No response_

### Which minecraft version are you using?

1.21

### On which mod loaders does it happen?

NeoForge

### Crash log

no crash

[comment by Mithi83 (collaborator)]
I think the problem is that the crafting plan is checked once before the start to determine which amount of what material must be reserved for the crafting job. But during the execution of the crafting plan any recipe for producing an intermediate will be exploited, even if that means that a resource is used that in theory should be reserved for another recipe. To avoid that the crafting plan would have to save the specific recipe used during planning rather than just the intended product/intermediate. Changing that could potentially have very serious side effects, as that code is a very complex and central part of the autocrafting.

I vaguely remember someone (Technici4n?) talk about something like that during the progress bar fix changes.

For your specific problem however I‘d suggest to disable substitution in the 1k storage component and make it regular certus only.

[comment by Mithi83 (collaborator)]
I would not go as far as to generally disable substitution. Substitution mode is still useful for other situations, e.g. to ignore durability in the cutting knifes for facades. As a heuristic in the AE2 area you could disable substitution for all recipes that allow certus quartz or charged certus quartz as an alternative.

If by „every type of board“ you mean the different types of wood, then maybe you don‘t want to use all types of wood to mass-craft chests if you only keep limited amounts of more rare types in stock for decorative purposes and have one farm that mass-produces oak logs for your regular crafting needs.

[comment by Mari023 (collaborator)]
It is only really problematic if you need a specific variant for some recipes, and any variant for others.
If you are only crafting chests, sticks and crafting tables, the exact wood types usually don't matter, and you can keep

If you are only crafting chests, sticks and crafting tables, the exact wood types usually don't matter, and you can keep substitutions on.

3. Put any random item in your off hand.
4. Attempt to load data from the block in step two with the memory card by shift right clicking.
5. Instead of the Memory Card being loaded with data from the block, get the error: "Could not load configuration from an incompatible device"

### Expected behavior

1. Get

title: Applied-Energistics-2 issue #8861: Remove co-processor limit for a single CraftingBlockEntity
text: [issue by Frostbite-time] ### Describe the feature I noticed that a few lines in `appeng.me.cluster.implementations.CraftingCPUCluster#addBlockEntity` cause the game to crash immediately when a `CraftingBlockEntity` with more than 16 co-processors becomes part of a Crafting CPU. I would like to remove this limitation. ### Reasons why it should be considered From the comment, I understand that this code was kept as a hard limit for lag mitigation. However, in practice, I do not think this limit has had a positive effect. For AE2 itself, there is currently only one `CraftingBlockEntity` with a co-processor count of 1, so this limit does not really do anything. For AE2 addons, this limit can simply be bypassed with a mixin, so it does not provide any real protection either. Instead, it has led quite a few people to mixin into this area, which increases the chance of mixin conflicts and causes more crashes. It also adds extra work for guys making AE2 addon mods. Even for performance itself, this limit does not necessarily have a positive effect: If the goal is to build a Crafting CPU with the same

title: Applied-Energistics-2 issue #8861: Remove co-processor limit for a single CraftingBlockEntity
text:
causes more crashes. It also adds extra work for guys making AE2 addon mods.

Even for performance itself, this limit does not necessarily have a positive effect:
If the goal is to build a Crafting CPU with the same total number of co-processors, using a single `CraftingBlockEntity` that provides more co-processors is usually better than using many blocks that each provide fewer co-processors. The latter requires more blocks to participate in multiblock detection, and multiblock detection itself also adds extra performance overhead.

### Additional details

On 1.21.1 and 1.20.1, many projects have already mixed into this code, so removing the limit suddenly there could also cause compatibility issues. However, for 26.1.2, I think this should not be a problem.

Also, just to be clear, I’m not a native English speaker, and I used AI to help translate this message, so the wording might sound a bit AI-generated 😅

title: Applied-Energistics-2 issue #9031: ME Storage Bus on Storage Controller showing double items
text:
er holding your Draconic Dust and Draconic Chunks by any chance a compacting drawer? Then this might mean you do not have enough Draconic Dust yet. Compacting Drawers are famous for reporting items twice (once all the Dusts that would be extractable and once all the Chunks that could be formed from the Dusts). There is no good solution for that. > I tried changing the render type as for that thread you suggested but I didn't notice any differences in behaviour.

Sodium 0.6 largely ignores the render type you assign, and tries to "downgrade" the render type if it determines the texture does not actually have alpha. But it will not "upgrade" the render type (either to enable alpha-testing or alpha-blending) for block models that didn't ask for it.

I'm pretty sure the bug that is affecting your mod exists in the render type downgrade logic.

title: sodium issue #3664: Driver workarounds are applied twice when FML early window control is disabled
text:
[issue by decce6]
### Bug Description

On NeoForge, when early window control is disabled, driver workarounds are applied twice, potentially causing error.

The first, in `GraphicsBootstrapper`:

https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/59e7586b49da6ba278912d03e8d83eef7a8b07d5/neoforge/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/service/SodiumWorkarounds.java#L23-L24

The second, in `WindowMixin`:

https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/59e7586b49da6ba278912d03e8d83eef7a8b07d5/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/mixin/workarounds/context_creation/WindowMixin.java#L40-L41

The root cause seems to be a change in NeoForge. On 1.21.1 the `glfwCreateWindow` call is [removed](https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/blob/869777fa2e6fc91b55a406e4b9733cb1dca92402/patches/com/mojang/blaze3d/platform/Window.java.patch#L7-L9), so the `WindowMixin` won't inject. On 1.21.11+, however, the `glfwCreateWindow` call [remains](https://github.com/neoforged/

title: sodium issue #3664: Driver workarounds are applied twice when FML early window control is disabled
text:
so the `WindowMixin` won't inject. On 1.21.11+, however, the `glfwCreateWindow` call [remains](https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/blob/6cb49467014c294e6cd6adae618d516a27c17cb5/patches/com/mojang/blaze3d/platform/Window.java.patch#L11) in place.

Note: This had been reported in https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/3636 but it was wrongly attributed to Ixeris or Async Logger.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Create a 1.21.11+ NeoForge instance and launch, for `fml.toml` to be created
2. In `fml.toml`, set `earlyWindowControl = false`
3. Install Sodium and launch the game
4. Observe that the driver workarounds are applied twice (the game might crash with message "Command line is already modified")

### Log File

Not needed (something similiar to "Modifying process environment to apply workarounds for the AMD graphics driver..." would be printed twice)

### Crash Report

See #3636

title: sodium issue #3703: [Crash] Crash with Create Big Cannons smoke particle render type on Sodium 0.8 1.21.1 backport
text:
[issue by rbasamoyai]

title: sodium issue #3810: Incompatible with NNP Fluidlogging
text:
Minecraft's code, it will not work with Sodium, and there is no way to avoid that.

If you are using the Fabric Rendering APIs, you can intercept block rendering and emit geometry as you'd like from your block models -- which is fully supported when using Sodium.

For the fluid renderer, this is more difficult (since the game hardcodes about everything), but Fabric still has an interface to hook fluid rendering (see [`FluidRenderHandler`](https://maven.fabricmc.net/docs/fabric-api-0.154.0+26.1.2/net/fabricmc/fabric/api/client/render/fluid/v1/FluidRenderHandler.html)) and allows you to emit geometry however you'd like. Please note however that it means you are responsible for providing the entire fluid renderer (maybe you can dispatch it to the modified-vanilla renderer if you _really_ want) and that has performance implications since you won't be using any of Sodium's code for it.

title: sodium issue #3810: Incompatible with NNP Fluidlogging
text:
all I need to do is replace instances of level#getBlockState#getFluidState with level#getFluidState. My other mixins will then query my neo chunk attachment. I really don't care about the rest of the rendering pipeline - I want to make as few changes as possible to whatever would happen if my mod weren't installed.

Edit: to put it another way: I'm not doing custom rendering, I'm just telling the game to render a different fluid.

[comment by jellysquid3 (member)]
Well, it is still possible to use the Fabric APIs on NeoForge, which is typically what we recommend to people instead of trying to mixin to our mod. If you don't want to do that, then options are limited since NeoForge doesn't provide a standard way of hooking this.

If you are extending the chunk data and need to access that data at mesh times, it will require modifications to [`LevelSlice`](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/dev/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/world/LevelSlice.java#L48). That class is responsible for copying all "relevant" world state for a given area into a buffer that can be used safely by other threads. It also implements the relevant interface (`BlockAndTintGetter`) that is then passed to every render function for querying block states, fluid states, etc.

How exactly you go about this is up to you, since with Mixins you are far outside any prescribed API.

> A problem with your hardware caused Windows to stop working correctly.

Windows is very plainly telling you that the NVIDIA graphics card in your computer is faulting. This is not a bug with Sodium or any other application. The fact that your computer enters "limp mode" after the hang is because the graphics driver has been unloaded, as the hardware device is in an unrecoverable state and the only way out is a complete reboot.

It may be the case that Sodium more easily provokes this issue, but that doesn't mean anything other than the particular workload is especially stressful on your hardware.

It could be a graphics driver bug, or simply that your hardware is faulty and becomes especially prone to crashing when temperatures get too hot.

title: Create issue #10340: The problem with infinite storage
text:
2026
**Minecraft Version:** 1.21.1
**Loader:** NeoForge 21.1.228
**Affected Mods:** Create (v0.6.10+), JEI/EMI

## 1. Issue Summary
A critical performance bottleneck has been identified when using the **Recipe Transfer** functionality (the "+" button in JEI/EMI) while sourcing materials from a **Create Creative Crate**. This results in a total server thread hang lasting between **800ms and 2500ms**, causing all world activities (machines, entities, sound processing) to freeze.

## 2. Technical Symptoms
- **MSPT Spike:** Server MSPT (Milliseconds Per Tick) jumps to **871ms+** during the interaction.
- **World Lock:** A complete "Server Thread Starvation" occurs. Mechanical animations from *Create* stop, and system audio associated with world ticks stutters or mutes.
- **Sync Blocking:** The issue is reproducible on both 1.20.1 and 1.21.1, suggesting a deep-rooted architectural conflict in how infinite inventory providers interact with the NeoForge/Forge Inventory API.

## 3. Profiler Analysis (Spark)
Spark profiler reports (Reference: [ZiSVwodFrh](https://spark.lucko.me/ZiSVwodFrh)) highlight the following:
- **Major Bottleneck:** `jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe.park()` occupying ~77-80% of the server thread.
- **Call Chain:** The hang originates during `RecipeTransferHandler` calls, specifically when the inventory provider (Creative Crate) is queried for item availability.
- **Sync Issues:** The

title: Create issue #10340: The problem with infinite storage
text:
Call Chain:** The hang originates during `RecipeTransferHandler` calls, specifically when the inventory provider (Creative Crate) is queried for item availability.
- **Sync Issues:** The profiler shows the server thread is stuck in `managedBlock` waiting for inventory data synchronization.

## 4. Steps to Reproduce
1. Place a **Creative Crate** from the *Create* mod and fill it with any crafting ingredient (e.g., iron ingots).
2. Open a crafting interface (Workbench or Terminal).
3. Search for a recipe requiring that ingredient in **JEI** or **EMI**.
4. Click the **"+" (Move Items)** button.
5. **Result:** The game client and server freeze for ~2 seconds.

## 5. Attempted Mitigations
- **Mod Pruning:** Removing heavy mods like *Quark* reduced background noise in the profiler but did **not** resolve the primary hang.
- **Inventory Buffering:** Using a standard chest as a buffer between the Creative Crate and the player resolves the lag, as the API no longer has to handle "Integer.MAX_VALUE" stack sizes during the transfer request.

## 6. Conclusion
The bug is a synchronous blocking request in the inventory transfer logic. The *Recipe Transfer API* fails to efficiently handle "infinite" inventory providers on NeoForge 1.21.1, leading to a hard thread lock.

---

I should firstly clarify that this is not a problem with the Chisels & Bits mod itself but instead a library it uses called [Scena](https://github.com/Communi-Suggestu/Scena).

Items can still be extracted normally from the GUI of the barrel by simply right-clicking the side of the Limited Barrel.

title: SophisticatedStorage issue #744: [BUG] NullPointerException Extracting Item from Storage with Compression Upgraded
text:
[issue by KhloeLeclair]
**Description**
Within [CompressionInventoryPart.extractItem](https://github.com/P3pp3rF1y/SophisticatedStorage/blob/1.21.x/src/main/java/net/p3pp3rf1y/sophisticatedstorage/upgrades/compression/CompressionInventoryPart.java#L298), the following line of code can throw a NullPointerException:
```java
int toExtract = Math.min(calculatedStacks.get(slot).getCount(), amount);
```

We believe this happened as a result of the amount of a stored item hitting zero when Create was trying to extract more than one thing at once (netherite blocks + netherite ingots, in this case, extracted via Packager upon request of a factory gauge) but I haven't been able to follow the logic enough to determine the exact cause yet.

Just to add from my side, I have added a few unit tests to make sure that extracting from incorrect slot - inaccessible marked with red cross - properly returns just empty stack and a test that extracts everything and then tries to continue extracting - like the case you mention above where netherite block is extracted and it then tries to extract netherite ingot which no longer exists - and that test also works properly and just returns empty. 
The reason this works properly is that when the last item is extracted the logic removes definitions for what items can go into what slot and how they compress and when no slot definition is present extract just immediately exits returning empty stack without checking anything else.

#### Versions (Be specific, do not write "latest"):
* Curios: 1.18.1-5.0.4.2
* Forge: 39.0.9
#### Observed Behavior:
- When in the vanilla inventory, if you click on the Curios button with an item, it will not carry over, but clicking it again to go back will restore the item to your cursor.
- When in the Curios inventory, if you click on the Curios button with an item, it will deposit the item straight into your first hotbar slot.
#### Expected Behavior:
- The item in your cursor should not be misplaced when clicking on the Curios button, which is how this behaved in the 1.16 version.
#### Steps to Reproduce:
1. When in either the vanilla or Curios inventory, grab an item from within the inventory.

Crash Log: No crash log or relevant logged information.

title: Curios issue #479: Glitch with multiple slots using the /add command
text:
nfromstatefarm (none)]
**After extensive testing, I have discovered a workaround for those encountering the same issue with the /curios add command.**

### **Avoid using SHIFT+CLICK to place items into Curios slots. Instead, drag and drop them directly.** 
It appears that using SHIFT+CLICK puts the items into slots that that are not rendered in the UI which cause the items to duplicate and seem like they have disappeared.

You can confirm this is the case by adding a ridiculous amount of slots (e.g., 300 or more), you'll find the items placed in those non-rendered slots. I should have figured this out earlier when playing with the SET command.

title: Curios issue #492: Incompatibility Between Curios API and Inventorio Mod Causing Crash in Minecraft 1.20.1
text:
[issue by icram0719]
There is an incompatibility between the Curios API and the Inventorio mod that results in a crash when both are installed in Minecraft 1.20.1. This prevents the game from functioning properly and affects players using these mods together.

Details:
Crash Occurrence: The game crashes during the common_setup event phase when both Curios and Inventorio are loaded.
Environment:
Minecraft Version: 1.20.1
Curios Version: curios-forge-5.12.1+1.20.1.jar
Inventorio Version: inventorio-mc1.20.1-forge-v1.10.3.jar

The crash generates an error related to the Curios API, and the game fails to proceed past initialization.

Similar issues have been noted by users on Reddit and Minecraft forums when combining Curios with other inventory-modifying mods, suggesting this is a broader compatibility challenge.

Steps to Reproduce
Install Minecraft 1.20.1 with Forge 
Add the Curios API mod .
Add the Inventorio mod .
Launch the game.
Observe the crash during the loading phase with an error referencing Curios.
Crash Log
[main/ERROR]:Mixin config entity_model_features.mixins.json does not specify "minVersion" property [main/ERROR]:com.electronwill.nightconfig.core.io.ParsingException: Not enough data available [main/ERROR]:com.electronwill.nightconfig.core.io.ParsingException: Not enough data available


Possible Causes
The crash appears to stem from a conflict between Curios and Inventorio, likely because both mods modify the game's inventory or equipment slot systems. This overlap may lead to conflicting code execution during initialization, causing the game to fail.

```
Mixin apply failed curios.mixins.json:MixinInventory -> net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Inventory: org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.transformer.throwables.InvalidMixinException @Shadow field f_35978_ was not located in the target class net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Inventory. In your `dependencies` block you have these lines:
```
compileOnly "top.theillusivec4.curios:curios-forge:${curios_version}:api"
runtimeOnly "top.theillusivec4.curios:curios-forge:${curios_version}"

- Mod version, 5.14.1+1.20.1

## Description of the Bug
I downloaded this mod as a dependency for [Elytra Slot](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/elytra-slot), loaded a survival world of mine with it, worked fine and as expected, was looking for a way to add more slots for things, found the curious API config and added a slot in the "Common" category. The slot that i added just had "Test" as its content.
I was unaware of the syntax as it was not described to me anywhere.
When i saved this, nothing really happened and i forgot about it. When i restarted my game and tried to load the same save game, i was greeted with screenshot 1 (see below), and when i tried to load the world in safe mode, i was met with screenshot 2.
When trying to create a new world, the game crashed (see crash log below).

## Steps to Reproduce
- Add a new slot in the config with faulty syntax.
- - Error: Load any save game
- - Crash: Click the "Create new world" button

## Note
I am aware that it is my fault i didnt real all readmes before trying stuff, but that doesnt take way from the fact that this error should never take place and instead should just warn the user that the slot they tried to add is incorrect.

[comment by BlayTheNinth (member)]
`Veinminer Client` is including an incompatible version of `fabric-permissions-api` for a newer version of Minecraft. Which is funny because on newer versions of Minecraft, the version they include is also incompatible, but instead for older versions of Minecraft.

The only way around this is reporting the issue to Veinminer Client, and either removing that mod or manually removing the wrong fabric-permissions-api jar from the Veinminer Client .jar.

title: Waystones issue #1203: Boat with passenger desyncs after waystone teleport — driver can't see the boat
text:
[issue by SukenFuyumi]
### Minecraft Version

1.21.1

### Mod Loader

Fabric (Loader 0.19.3)

### Mod Version

21.1.36+fabric-1.21.1 (Balm 21.0.62)

### Describe the Issue

On a dedicated multiplayer server, two players riding the **same vanilla boat** teleport via a waystone. Both players are teleported correctly, but the boat desyncs: the **driver** (the one who activated the waystone) no longer sees the boat, while the **passenger** still sees it. Appears to be the same client-side entity desync as #402 / #718 (entity teleports but fails to render on one client).

**Reproduction:**
1. Player A (driver) + Player B (passenger) in one vanilla boat.
2. Player A activates a waystone and teleports.
3. Both arrive; Player A's client no longer renders the boat, Player B still sees it.

Consistent. No crash — purely a visual/entity desync, nothing logged.

### Performance/other mods

Yes — this is a large Cobblemon modpack (Cobbleverse) including Sodium, Lithium, C2ME, EntityCulling and ModernFix, so a client render/culling interaction can't be fully ruled out.

[comment by BlayTheNinth (member)]
This seems to actually apply to all entities that are teleported (except items and players). If the other player in the faraway target area doesn't have the entities tracked, they're going to be invisible, even when teleporting them through Vanilla means (e.g. `/tp @e[type=don

text:
in the faraway target area doesn't have the entities tracked, they're going to be invisible, even when teleporting them through Vanilla means (e.g. `/tp @e[type=donkey] @s`). So it appears to be a Vanilla bug.

I will see if I can find a workaround.

Crash when trying to see any Iron's Spell and Spellbooks enchanted armor. When hovering in inventory (using a mod that renders armor from hovering on it) cause severe lag and when equipped it crashes every player seeing it.

Equip and see the armor on.

Take any Iron's Spell and Spellbooks' armor, enchant it, and hover it or equip it, after that, try to look at it with third person, from inventory or from another player perspective -> client who tries this crashes.

Third part hosted server (but I guess also singleplayer, not tested though).

forge 47.4.0

## Bug Report: NullPointerException in GeoArmorRenderer when checking entity glow status

### Description
Game crashes when rendering armor on entities due to a null entity being passed to `shouldEntityAppearGlowing()` method in `GeoArmorRenderer.java` line 333.

### Minecraft Version
- **Minecraft**: 1.21.1
- **NeoForge**: 21.1.216
- **GeckoLib**: 4.8.2 (geckolib-neoforge-1.21.1-4.8.2.jar)

### Crash Location
```
at software.bernie.geckolib.renderer.GeoArmorRenderer.renderToBuffer(GeoArmorRenderer.java:333)
at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.shouldEntityAppearGlowing(Minecraft.java:2609)
```

### Root Cause
The `GeoArmorRenderer.renderToBuffer()` method at line 333 calls `Minecraft.getInstance().shouldEntityAppearGlowing(entity)` without checking if the entity parameter is null first.

### Error Message
```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity.isCurrentlyGlowing()" because "p_91315_" is null
```

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Join a multiplayer server with GeckoLib-based armor mods installed
2. Navigate to the Nether dimension
3. Encounter Zombified Piglins wearing modded armor
4. Game crashes when trying to render the enti

title: geckolib issue #804: NullPointerException in GeoArmorRenderer when checking entity glow status
text:
Join a multiplayer server with GeckoLib-based armor mods installed
2. Navigate to the Nether dimension
3. Encounter Zombified Piglins wearing modded armor
4. Game crashes when trying to render the entity

### Affected Entities
- Zombified Piglins (minecraft:zombified_piglin)
- Likely affects any mob wearing GeckoLib-based armor

### Mods Involved
- **Immersive Armors** 1.7.5
- **Advanced Netherite** 2.3.1
- **Ars Nouveau** 5.10.6 (uses entity lighting system)
- **Accessories** mod (involved in armor rendering pipeline)

### Expected Behavior
The renderer should gracefully handle null entities without crashing.

### Suggested Fix
Add a null check in `GeoArmorRenderer.renderToBuffer()` before calling glow methods:
```java
// Line 333 in GeoArmorRenderer.java
if (entity != null && Minecraft.getInstance().shouldEntityAppearGlowing(entity)) {
    // ... glow rendering code
}
```

### Additional Context
- Crash occurs consistently at specific coordinates in the Nether
- Happens during armor layer rendering (`HumanoidArmorLayer.render`)
- The crash persists even after disabling dynamic lighting features in client mods
- Multiple other mods are applying mixins to the armor rendering pipeline (Accessories, Iris, etc.)

### Environment
- **OS**: Windows 11
- **Java**: OpenJDK 21.0.9
- **Graphics**: AMD Radeon RX 7600

title: geckolib issue #846: Animation time appears quantized to 0.5-tick on non-Entity renderers (MC 26.1.2)
text:
[issue by rayfilm0815]
## Body

Hi GeckoLib team — thanks for maintaining this, it's been a huge help on our project.

While debugging a "low-FPS-looking" animation at 200+ render FPS on a custom `GeoItemRenderer`, we think we traced it to how `DataTickets.TICK` is populated on non-Entity render states. Posting in case it's unintentional or worth a look; happy to close if it's by design.

### Environment

- GeckoLib 26.1.2
- Minecraft 26.1.2 (Fabric)
- Custom `GeoItemRenderer` subclass (the same pattern also reproduces on a `GeoObjectRenderer`)

### Observed behavior

On a plain `GeoRenderState` (Item / ObjectRenderer path — anything that doesn't land on `EntityRenderStateMixin.getAnimatableAge`), `renderState.getAnimatableAge()` advances in 0.5-tick steps (e.g. `…963.5, 963.5, 964.0, 964.0, 964.0, 964.5, …`) even at 200 render FPS.

The `partialTick` parameter passed into `addRenderData(..., float partialTick)` is frame-smooth in the same frames (multiple distinct values per tick, matching `DeltaTracker.getGameTimeDeltaPartialTick(false)` when sampled right there).

Downstream effect: `AnimationController.checkControllerState` computes `timeDelta` from `getAnimatableAge()` → `timelineTime`, `

title: geckolib issue #846: Animation time appears quantized to 0.5-tick on non-Entity renderers (MC 26.1.2)
text:
when sampled right there).

Downstream effect: `AnimationController.checkControllerState` computes `timeDelta` from `getAnimatableAge()` → `timelineTime`, `animationPoint.animTime` all step at 0.025s → bone output quantizes to ~40 Hz regardless of render FPS, making all animations look choppy.

### Suspected cause: inconsistent `ignoreFrozenGame` flag

`GeoRendererInternals.captureDefaultRenderState` (L83–84):

```java
if (!DataTickets.TICK.canExtractFrom(renderState))
    renderState.addGeckolibData(DataTickets.TICK, ClientUtil.getCurrentTick());
```

`ClientUtil.getCurrentTick()` (L53–59):

```java
return mc.level != null ?
    mc.level.getGameTime() + mc.getDeltaTracker().getGameTimeDeltaPartialTick(false) :
    Blaze3D.getTime() * 20d;
```

Meanwhile, `GeckolibItemSpecialRenderer.buildRenderState` (L81–82) calls `fillRenderState` with:

```java
Minecraft.getInstance().getDeltaTracker().getGameTimeDeltaPartialTick(true)
```

So within a single `fillRenderState` call chain:
- `DataTickets.PARTIAL_TICK` ends up storing the `ignoreFrozenGame=true` value (the `partialTick` parameter)
- `

rayfilm0815 (none)]
Hi Tslat,

I've updated to **26.2 / GeckoLib 5.5.3** and the animation issue is still present. After further testing, I believe the root cause is related to **world `gameTime` accumulation** and **`float` precision loss**.

**Observed behavior:** The longer a world has been running, the worse the animation tick resolution becomes. On our server, the effective animation tick rate has degraded to roughly **1–4 ticks** of perceived update frequency. Switching immediately to a fresh singleplayer world restores smooth animation — confirming this is `gameTime`-dependent, not a framerate issue.

---

## Root cause analysis

The expression in `ClientUtil.getCurrentTick()`:

```java
mc.level.getGameTime() + partialTick
```

performs a **`long + float → float`** promotion under JLS binary numeric promotion rules. Since `float` only has a **24-bit mantissa**, once `gameTime > 2^24` (approximately **9.3 real-time days of game time**), `partialTick` becomes smaller than 1 ULP of the result and is **silently discarded** by the addition — `DataTickets.TICK` stops advancing between ticks, freezing animations.

**Live sample from our server (2026-06-22):**
`gameTime = 477,945,762` — `TICK` reported the same value (`4.7794576E8 = 477,945,760`) across **8 consecutive frames**.

title: geckolib issue #891: `[1.21.1] Client crash "IllegalStateException: Not building!" when a glowing GeckoLib entity is hit (stale outline buffer reference)`
text:
[issue by SpaceOddityTr]
**Environment:** Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.248, GeckoLib 4.9.2, Mowzie's Mobs 1.8.2 (renderer in the stack, but the mechanism is GeckoLib-generic).

**Reproduction (3/3 on our pack):**
1. Summon a GeckoLib-rendered entity (observed with `mowziesmobs:umvuthi`).
2. Give it the Glowing effect (in the wild, Umvuthi's healers apply it as a game mechanic).
3. Hit the entity (melee or gunfire) while its outline is on screen.
4. Client crashes:

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Not building!
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.BufferBuilder.ensureBuilding(BufferBuilder.java:76)
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.BufferBuilder.addVertex(BufferBuilder.java:156)
  at net.minecraft.client.renderer.OutlineBufferSource$EntityOutlineGenerator.addVertex(OutlineBufferSource.java:58)
  at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.VertexMultiConsumer$Double.addVertex(VertexMultiConsumer.java:79)  (x2)
  at software.bernie.geckolib.renderer.GeoRenderer.createVerticesOfQuad(GeoRenderer.java:341)
  at software.bernie.geckolib.renderer.GeoRenderer.renderCube(GeoRenderer.java:328)
  at com.bobmowzie.mowzie

title: geckolib issue #891: `[1.21.1] Client crash "IllegalStateException: Not building!" when a glowing GeckoLib entity is hit (stale outline buffer reference)`
text:
er.java:341)
  at software.bernie.geckolib.renderer.GeoRenderer.renderCube(GeoRenderer.java:328)
  at com.bobmowzie.mowziesmobs.client.render.entity.MowzieGeoEntityRenderer.renderRecursively(...)
```

Notably, Glowing **alone does not crash** — we tested a glowing Umvuthana and a glowing vanilla cow standing idle. The crash requires a hit landing while the outline is rendered.

**Mechanism (verified against 1.21.1 bytecode):**

* Vanilla `OutlineBufferSource` backs all glow outlines with **one shared immediate `BufferSource`**; requesting a different `RenderType` from an immediate source **ends the previous builder**.
* `GeoRenderer` fetches the (outline-wrapping) `VertexConsumer` once and holds it across the whole bone pass.
* When the hit lands, something re-enters the same outline source with another render type mid-pass (hurt overlay / held item / a render layer — the exact trigger doesn't change the picture). The shared builder is ended; GeckoLib keeps writing through the stale `EntityOutlineGenerator` reference; the next `addVertex` throws.

**Suggested fix:** re-fetch the buffer from the `MultiBufferSource` whenever the render type can have changed within the bone pass (or per bone/cube batch), instead of holding one `VertexConsumer` across code that may switch render types. Alternatively, catching the ended-builder state before writing would make the outline path

title: ModernFix issue #454: Dynamic Resources changes the behaviour of Fabric Api's `getModel()`
text:
[issue by Estecka]
### Bug Description

The class `ModelManager` has two different overloads for `getModel`:   
The vanilla implementation takes a `ModelResourceLocation` as argument, and falls back to returning a missing model.  
Fabric Api's implementation takes a plain `ResourceLocation` as argument, and falls back to returning `null`.

When ModernFix's Dynamic Resources is enabled, Fabric Api's overload returns a missing model instead of null, which can throw off mods that rely on detecting missing models.

The context for this is similar to #433, but involves a different overload of `getModel`. This time it will be trivial to work around this on my end, so there's no urgency to fix this, but I still thought this behaviour was worth documenting.
(And honnestly I have no idea why those two behave differently to begin with. I might just take this issue to Fabric Api as well.)

### Reproduction Steps

- Install [Enchants-CIT v1.0.0](https://modrinth.com/mod/enchants-cit/version/1.0.0+1.21)
- Search for enchanted books with the newest enchantments (e.g windburst)
   - Without Dynamic Resources: the item uses the vanilla texture.
   - With Dynamic Resources: the item has a missing texture.

The model loading code in vanilla has changed drastically between 1.20.1 and now, and requires more aggressive patches to support dynamically loading and unloading the models. Will copy the relevant text of my announcement on Discord, as I realized it's not visible to anyone not in the server:

> That leaves the obvious final question of "where is 1.21.5, and what are you planning for 1.22?" The answer is: I need a break from porting this mod. I've had to dedicate a substantial amount of time to port to minor updates while ultimately throwing out that code due to future changes. This isn't sustainable and it's taken time away from being able to work on new features (case in point - most ModernFix features on 1.20 are just ports of code developed during the 1.19 lifecycle).
Whether or not it's better to port to the latest versions as they come out or stick to a quasi-"LTS" is a hotly contested topic in the community. But for ModernFix specifically, I think the latter is more beneficial to the playerbase overall, so I'm simply not going to be porting to 1.21.5 or any of the minor versions until I see the community settle on a new version for modpacks. The code is as always open source, so others are free to port to those minor versions if they're interested, and I won't stop them.

title: ModernFix issue #595: MSPT graph in F3 shows wrong color for idle time
text: ; regardless of positive, neutral, or negative performance effects and optimisation of this mod, TPS should always be limited to 20 no matter what. If your TPS graph is showing an upper bound that does _not_ read as 20.0, then you've either run `/tick rate `, a datapack has, or a mod has. At 20 TPS, you will have 50 _MSPT_ though. 50 ms per tick gives 20 ticks a second, with the graph showing red for tick processing time, and green as the rest of the time spent waiting (to maintain 20 TPS max). If the red part exceeds 50 ms, then the green (waiting) part won't happen because the tick will be taking >50 MSPT and therefore the TPS will be _below_ 20 and the server should be catching up, not waiting. AFAIK, there's nothing that modifies this behaviour in this mod, because this is just very core Vanilla mechanics that no mod usually touches. `/tick rate` and other mods/datapacks that explicitly aim at changing the tick rate are generally the only things that call on deviating from the assumed Vanilla mechanic of _20 TPS max (∴ 50 max MSPT) and if a tick takes <1,000÷TPS ms to process, wait, otherwise don't_. When loading a large pack, the game crashes during the `net.neoforged.neoforge.registries.RegisterEvent`. The error indicates that the item registration has been accelerated too aggressively, causing key mods to crash upon self-referencing an item that has not yet been fully bound by the system.

    mixin.feature.registry_event_progress=false
    ```

title: ModernFix issue #619: Integrated server watchdog not sending thread dump when server thread stalls in a certain save
text:
[issue by Appulcake]
### Bug Description

This issue report is related to a user in FTB Discord having trouble loading their save.
Context is modpack FTB Stoneblock 4 (1.4.0), using MC 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.216, ModernFix version `modernfix-neoforge-5.25.1+mc1.21.1`, when loading a (certain) save in Single Player.
Pack comes with a `modernfix-mixins.properties` shipped by default overriding one entry (`mixin.perf.model_optimizations=false`), not touching `mixin.feature.integrated_server_watchdog` from default of true.

There's an issue caused by Irregular Implements mod in the pack that under certain conditions indefinitely stalls the server thread on save load (https://github.com/FTBTeam/FTB-Modpack-Issues/issues/10755). This is usually quickly recognised in crash assistant reports, as ModernFix does an integrated server thread dump normally on this stall, where it becomes quickly obvious that it's this issue based on where the Server Thread is stuck. In this case, updating irregular implements fixes this issue.

However, for this one user's save, this doesn't happen. I could reproduce this, using Java `21.0.4+7-LTS` (bundled by FTB App), user had it happen on `21.0.7+6-LTS`, and then me again on `21.0.9`. I had to get a thread dump by doing a `jstack` output on it.

When I added a `mixin.feature.spam_thread_dump=true` override to `modernfix-

title: ModernFix issue #619: Integrated server watchdog not sending thread dump when server thread stalls in a certain save
text:
had to get a thread dump by doing a `jstack` output on it.

When I added a `mixin.feature.spam_thread_dump=true` override to `modernfix-mixins.properties`, it successfully does a thread dump every minute, including after this stall, in which the Server Thread is all stuck on Timed Waiting, so it seems capable of doing a dump it's just not triggering to do it for some reason despite the indefinite stall.

### Reproduction Steps

Unfortunately, I don't know what's different about this user's save that doesn't trigger this behaviour, that all previous saves with this issue do normally trigger a thread dump for.

I've included the user's save here (deleted other dimensions + trimmed down their dimension to reduce save file size, while still able to reproduce the issue): [New World.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24194416/New.World.zip)

title: ModernFix issue #619: Integrated server watchdog not sending thread dump when server thread stalls in a certain save
text:
Latest.log (Tail)](https://gnomebot.dev/paste/mclogs/0r5Laab) (part of user's original report)

[comment by embeddedt (owner)]
I believe this is by design. The integrated server watchdog is started after the server finishes initializing (i.e. the initial chunks have loaded, but the client may not have joined the world yet). A side effect of this is that it cannot capture deadlocks that happen during the initial chunkload. `mixin.perf.spam_thread_dump=true` is the recommended workaround in such situations, as it is not dependent on monitoring the server's "next tick time" data to capture thread information.

Enabling the watchdog earlier will almost certainly result in a lot of false positive messages because there is no real ticking happening yet, and the chunkloading can take quite some time especially on weak systems.

I would guess that in cases where it does happen to work, spawn chunk preloading is disabled, so the server has technically begun ticking at the point that it loads the problematic chunk.

This crash log is particularly hard to decipher, because the crash originates from here:

```
Caused by: java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class malte0811.ferritecore.mixin.config.FerriteConfig
...
Caused by: java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError: Exception java.lang.RuntimeException: java.lang.reflect.InvocationTargetException [in thread "main"]
	at TRANSFORMER/ferritecore@6.0.1/malte0811.ferritecore.mixin.config.FerriteConfig$ConfigBuilder.finish(FerriteConfig.java:100)

	at TRANSFORMER/ferritecore@6.0.1/malte0811.ferritecore.mixin.predicates.Config.<init>(Config.java:8)
```

This appears because `FerriteConfig` tries to reflectively invoke a method, and then immediately wrap any exceptions thrown in a `RuntimeException`, it hides the underlying cause (which would be whatever error was thrown in the reflectively invoked method itself:

https://github.com/malte0811/FerriteCore/blob/e47bcbbde5

title: FerriteCore issue #164: Crash on startup - `FerriteConfig` hides exceptions raised in `ConfigFileHandler` by not unwrapping the underlying `InvocationTargetException`
text:
underlying cause (which would be whatever error was thrown in the reflectively invoked method itself:

https://github.com/malte0811/FerriteCore/blob/e47bcbbde5b83805f927bad82bcc2b323e7169b8/Common/src/main/java/malte0811/ferritecore/mixin/config/FerriteConfig.java#L94-L101

Ideally, this should catch `InvocationTargetException`s, and throw a `new RuntimeError(e.getCause())`, as that would be the actual underlying error being thrown. Beyond that, FerriteCore is crashing on startup here with unclear cause, but the problem _appears_ to be directly related to whatever `ConfigFileHandler` is doing, which seems to crash loading the mixin config plugin.

I reported this issue because there _is_ a very obvious problem here, namely the `catch(Exception e) { throw new RuntimeException(e); }`, should be catching `InvocationTargetException` and rethrowing the `e.getTargetException()` - the exception that actually occurred in the reflective access - which would make this issue, if it were to appear again, at least _visible_.

What made my test log hard to follow was that the exception did not trigger a crash immediately, instead some later similar exception did. Changing the exception structure would not affect that. [comment by malte0811 (owner)]
You seem to be using a mod that allows (Neo?)Forge mods to be loaded on Fabric. Are you using the Fabric versions of Lithium and FerriteCore, or did you install the (Neo?)Forge version of one or both? What MC version are you on? Lithium and FC both modify the same data structures by default, so they need to "communicate" with each other during launch. To my knowledge this works very well when both are expecting the same loader, but since this communication is heavily based on the loader it probably will not work across "mixed" versions (or, for that matter, probably even when both are expecting Neo/Forge). If that is not the problem, please upload a full log. This is not enough data to go on here.

FerriteCore issue #219: Client startup extremely slow (400+ seconds) when FerriteCore and Supplementaries are both installed (NeoForge 1.21.1)
text:
[issue by Esteban-Chielens]
### Summary

I’m running into a very large client startup slowdown (400+ seconds) that only occurs when **FerriteCore** and **Supplementaries** are both installed on NeoForge 1.21.1. As soon as FerriteCore is removed, startup times return to normal.

### Environment

* Minecraft: **NeoForge 1.21.1**
* Base modpack: **Optimized FPS (Modrinth)**, used as a starting point
* Issue occurs on the **client**, during startup (before the main menu)
* System resources don’t appear to be the bottleneck (CPU/RAM usage remains normal during the hang)

### What Happens

* **Supplementaries + FerriteCore enabled**

  * Client startup takes **400+ seconds**
  * No clear errors or warnings in the logs
* **Supplementaries enabled, FerriteCore disabled**

  * Startup time is normal
* **FerriteCore enabled, Supplementaries disabled**

  * Startup time is normal

Because each mod works fine on its own, this looks like an interaction issue rather than a standalone bug in either mod.

### Profiling Results

I profiled client startup using Spark. The vast majority of the time is spent in:

```
net.minecraft.client.resources.model.BlockStateModelLoader
```

Specifically during **blockstate model loading**.

* Without Supplementaries: [https://spark.lucko.me/HSeULPjj0e](https://spark.lucko.me/HSeULPjj0e)
* With Supplementaries: [https://spark.lucko.me/73wz1AxJ5f](https://spark

* Average blockstates per block: **18.74**

These numbers were reviewed by the Supplementaries developer and considered normal. This suggests the slowdown isn’t due to an unusually large number of blocks or blockstates, but rather how they’re being processed during model loading.

### Troubleshooting So Far

* Did a binary search through mods → disabling **FerriteCore** consistently fixes the issue
* Tried disabling performance/render-related mods with no change:

  * Embeddium / Sodium
  * ETF / EMF
  * Fusion (connected textures)
* Logs don’t show anything obvious that explains the delay:
  [https://mclo.gs/mgN0DoL](https://mclo.gs/mgN0DoL)

### Expected Behavior

FerriteCore shouldn’t introduce extreme client startup delays when used with common content mods like Supplementaries, especially since both are widely used together in performance-focused modpacks.

### Thoughts / Hypothesis

My guess is that some FerriteCore optimization path (possibly related to deduplication, caching, or model handling) is interacting poorly with Supplementaries during the client model

title: JustEnoughItems issue #4163: [Bug]: [1.21.10 Fabric] Crash on load due to non-ASCII character in Grindstone Disenchantment Recipe ID
text:
[issue by vfggf95565]
### Steps to Reproduce the Bug

1.  Use Minecraft version `1.21.10`.
2.  Use Fabric Loader version `0.17.3` or later.
3.  Include **Just Enough Items (JEI)** version `26.1.0.16` (or later) along with the attached list of mods.
4.  Launch the game (client-side or server-side).

The crash occurs during the recipe registration phase, specifically when JEI attempts to generate/register Grindstone Disenchantment recipes. The crash is consistently reproducible on load.

### Expected Behavior

The game should load successfully, and JEI should register all recipes (including Grindstone Disenchantment recipes) without encountering any errors related to invalid characters in `ResourceLocations`.

### Actual Behavior

The game crashes immediately during the loading phase due to a `Packet handling error`. The specific error points to an invalid character (`\u0661` - Arabic-Indic digit '1') in the `ResourceLocation` of a Grindstone disenchantment recipe, as seen in the stack trace originating from `mezz.jei.library.plugins.vanilla.grindstone.GrindstoneRecipeMaker`.

**Error Location:**
`net.minecraft.class_151: Non [a-z0-9/._-] character in path of location: minecraft:grindstone.disenchantment.item.minecraft.wooden_shovel.efficiency.\u0661`

### Mod Pack URL (Optional)

_No response_

### Mod Pack Version (Optional)

Minecraft: `1.21.10` Mod Loader: `Fabric - 26.1.0

### Extra Notes (Optional)

The crash is caused by an invalid character (the Arabic-Indic digit **`\u0661`** which represents the number **"1"**) being used in a `ResourceLocation` path for a Grindstone disenchantment recipe.

The invalid ID is:
`minecraft:grindstone.disenchantment.item.minecraft.wooden_shovel.efficiency.\u0661`

This error occurs deep within the JEI codebase (`mezz.jei.library.plugins.vanilla.grindstone.GrindstoneRecipeMaker`), suggesting that either:

1.  JEI is incorrectly generating a recipe ID containing this character.
2.  Or, another installed mod is introducing an enchantment/item level (`Efficiency \u0661`) that causes JEI's recipe generation logic to fail.

I have already attempted switching the game language to English, but the issue persists, indicating the character is hardcoded or generated, not user-inputted.

[issue by jim139129]
### Steps to Reproduce the Crash

1. Install NeoForge 1.21.1 with JEI, Create, and Farmer's Delight.
2. Open the inventory to access JEI.
3. Look up the "Spout" block from Create and check its "Uses" (Right-click).
4. Navigate to the "Spout Filling" tab.
5. The first page of recipes renders correctly.
6. Click the arrow to navigate to the **2nd page** of recipes.
7. The game crashes immediately.

I have isolated this to a minimal instance with only Create, JEI, and Farmer's Delight. Removing Farmer's Delight stops the crash.

### Mod Pack Version (Optional)

While I understand the root cause likely lies within Create (attempting to access an empty fluid list index) or a malformed recipe from Farmer's Delight, I am reporting it here in hopes that JEI could potentially catch this exception during the recipe rendering phase. 

Ideally, a single malformed recipe render should not crash the entire client, but rather display an error placeholder for that specific entry if possible.

title: JustEnoughItems issue #4319: [Crash]: Crashes when oppening config icon in the creative menu
text:
The failure path is:
1. JEI cannot open an in-game config screen, so it displays a local message containing an `OPEN_FILE` link to the config folder.
2. FancyMenu 3.9.1 intercepts and serializes that message.
3. Minecraft rejects serializing the client-only `OPEN_FILE` action, producing `JsonParseException: Action not allowed: OPEN_FILE`.

Please report this issue to `FancyMenu` and link back to this issue in case they have questions or need support.

[comment by mezz (owner)]
It looks like this was already reported as FancyMenu [#1628](https://github.com/Keksuccino/FancyMenu/issues/1628) and fixed. The fix first shipped for Minecraft 1.21.1 in FancyMenu 3.9.7

title: JustEnoughItems issue #4498: [Crash]: Create 6.0.10 Causes JEI 19.56.0.441 Crash
text:
[issue by Bopkasen]
### Steps to Reproduce the Crash

Based on the log file you provided, the problem with JEI is a hard code conflict with the Create mod (create-1.21.1-6.0.10.jar).

The critical crash error preventing JEI from indexing ingredients on world join is:

`java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: An interpreter is already registered for this: create:potion`

Why this is happening:

Both Create and another active mod are trying to register a sub-type interpreter for fluid potions (`create:potion`) inside the JEI registry map simultaneously. Java does not allow double-registrations on the same hook, forcing JEI to throw an `IllegalArgumentException` and lock up.

### Mod Pack URL (Optional)

_No response_

### Mod Pack Version (Optional)

_No response_

### Extra Notes (Optional)

Codename Ancient Builder X3 preparing a modpack for a server host owner expecting 50+ players to play this

### Crash Report

https://gist.github.com/Bopkasen/3d5a2e8de1fe59048ff37fb3fa1e43bb

How to Fix It

Fix 1: Step down your primary JEI version (Recommended)You are currently running jei-1.21.1-neoforge-19.56.0.441.jar. The 19.56.x branch altered how custom fluid registries are handled.

Close your game entirely.

Navigate to your ATLauncher instance folder: 📂 config/almostunified/unification/.Open the mods/ directory and delete jei-1.21.1-neoforge-19.56.0.441.jar.

Download and install Just Enough Items (

: 📂 config/almostunified/unification/.Open the mods/ directory and delete jei-1.21.1-neoforge-19.56.0.441.jar.

Download and install Just Enough Items (JEI) version 19.21.0.166 (or any build in the stable 19.21.x milestone branch for 1.21.1). 

This step-down will safely parse the duplicate fluid tags without crashing the engine.

Fix 2: Add Create Potions to your Almost Unified Exclusions

Since the fluid collision is overlapping with your unification data maps, you can use your common.json file that you configured earlier to make the unification engine completely ignore the potion conflict:

Open 📂 config/almostunified/common.json.Locate the "ignored_items": [] array block.

Register the create potion item reference inside the brackets: "ignored_items": ["create:potion"].

[comment by double-pi (none)]
@FlashHUN how did u fix it? What does it mean "excluding KFF's transitive dependency"?

[comment by c-Caelum (none)]
I assume you've either solved it or given up at this point, but in build files, we have something called transitive dependencies. These basically mean that a project you depend on (for example `example-mod`) needs something, and so it passes it onto your project. `exclude` lets you manually get rid of one of these transitive dependencies, like so:
```gradle
implementation("my-example-mod-dependency:1.0") {
    exclude group: "my.example.exclusion.group", module "moduleToExclude"
}
```

title: KotlinForForge issue #110: [1.21.1-Neoforge] EventBusSubscriber Annotation doesn't work on Java class
text:
[issue by alegian]
I want to integrate KFF into a large codebase incrementally. I was happy to see that the `@Mod` annotation works for my main Java mod class, even when using KFF loader. 

I expected the `@EventBusSubscriber` annotation to do the same on my events class (uses **static** methods), but it doesn't. It doesn't even complain, Neo just crashes because of unregistered stuff. Switching my event class to Kotlin object immediately solved it.

I don't know how KFF works, so I dont know if this is feasible, but it should definitely be documented somewhere. I spent hours debugging it, since there is no visible KFF error. The skeleton projects have no dedicated event file example.

To be clear, the issue is: Following the steps in README for an existing mod, the resulting setup may sometimes crash, due to events not being loaded.

title: KotlinForForge issue #90: Crash in dev on NeoForge 20.4.40-beta (and later) due to changes in mods.toml
text:
[issue by Prototik]
In 20.4.40 NeoForge made changes in mods.toml format (see more [on their discord](https://discord.com/channels/313125603924639766/437004041394847745/1185682777245499412) or in [commit description](https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/commit/8786a13b2191ece3265e3c4de9517a7c2f572d3d)), and deprecated `mandatory` field in flavor of `type` field with `required`/`optional` values.
And made it hard failure in dev (dumbest thing I have ever seen, but who cares).

So KFF (which still uses `mandatory` field) no longer possible to use with latest Neo in Dev runtime, but in Prod it works just fine.

Please look on the Mixin Errors on Debug. Thanks

latest.log Client

[comment by gliscowo (member)]
Judging from how verbose this log is about mixin applications, I suspect the problem is that you used the `-Dmixin.debug=true` flag (or some variant of it) which forces very strict validation for all injections. This also changes behavior (likely in ways you didn't intend) and breaks the perfectly valid pair of Fabric/Quilt-specific injections of which only one must succeed under normal circumstances due to being grouped.

yeah, it was a problem with the debugin from mixin, but now it work again, had only searched an bug and it got me the owo bug also

It's not caused by another mod. NeoForge itself loads `CompoundTag` and `ComponentSerialization` early via `ImmediateWindowHandler$DummyProvider.updateModuleReads()` → `Class.forName()` during game layer acceptance, before the mixin sub

title: owo-lib issue #455: [1.21.1] DataResult is class loaded to early causing a crash
text:
ponentSerialization` early via `ImmediateWindowHandler$DummyProvider.updateModuleReads()` → `Class.forName()` during game layer acceptance, before the mixin subsystem processes any configs. This happens with owo-lib as the only mod installed.

The affected mixins are:
- `NbtCompoundMixin` → `net.minecraft.nbt.CompoundTag`
- `text.TextCodecsMixin` → `net.minecraft.network.chat.ComponentSerialization`

Additionally, the **accessories** mod has its own `temp_fixes.NbtCompoundMixin` targeting `CompoundTag` with the same crash.

This blocks the entire owo → accessories → mega evolution chain on NeoForge dedicated servers (Mega Showdown, ZA Megas, Horret's Extended Megas, Starlight Fusion).

Marking this wontfix means owo-lib's NeoForge port is unusable on dedicated servers. The root cause is in NeoForge's bootstrap, but the fix would need to come from owo-lib by either not mixing into these early-loaded classes or finding an alternative approach.

```java

```

In this case the missing keys are `registry_name` and `registry_key` inside the `cold_sweat:armor_insulation` component, which are only written when the insulator comes from a registry.

    if (input != null && input.value() instanceof String value) return DataResult.success(value);
    return DataResult.error(() -> "Not a string: " + input);
}
```

title: owo-lib issue #507: [1.21.1 NeoForge] NeoForge 21.1.262 breaks NetworkRegistryMixin (RETURN ordinal = 3): "Sided Packet Codec has not been unpacked", every player kicked on join
text:
[issue by oggioni2004]
**Versions:** owo-lib 0.12.15.5-beta.1+1.21 (NeoForge), Accessories 1.1.0-beta.53+1.21.1, Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge **21.1.262** (works on 21.1.259)

**What happens:** on NeoForge 21.1.262, every player is disconnected while joining a dedicated server:
```
Internal Exception: io.netty.handler.codec.EncoderException: Failed to encode packet 'clientbound/minecraft:custom_payload'
Failed encoding custom payload accessories:main: [owo] Sided Packet Codec has not been unpacked
```

**Cause:** `io.wispforest.owo.mixin.neoforge.NetworkRegistryMixin#owo$unpackSidedCodec` targets `NetworkRegistry.getCodec` with `@At(value = "RETURN", ordinal = 3)`.

NeoForge commit neoforged/NeoForge@0e98dad, shipped in 21.1.262 ("Enforce network setup payload directions and decoding limits"), added a new early `return null` inside the `BUILTIN_PAYLOADS` branch of that method. The RETURN ordinals in 21.1.262 are now:

| ordinal | return |
|---|---|
| 0 | `return null` (new: serverbound modded setup payloads) |
| 1 | `return BUILTIN_PAYLOADS.get(id)` |
| 2 | `return null` (no registration) |
| 3 |

title: owo-lib issue #507: [1.21.1 NeoForge] NeoForge 21.1.262 breaks NetworkRegistryMixin (RETURN ordinal = 3): "Sided Packet Codec has not been unpacked", every player kicked on join
text:

| 1 | `return BUILTIN_PAYLOADS.get(id)` |
| 2 | `return null` (no registration) |
| 3 | `return null` (flow mismatch) ← owo now modifies this one |
| 4 | `return registration.codec()` ← should be modified |
| 5 | `return null` (wrong phase) |

As a result, the `SidedPacketCodec` is never unpacked, and its `encode`/`decode` always throw. This breaks Accessories and every mod using owo networking on NeoForge 1.21.1. Hosts that auto-update the loader (for example Aternos) can't pin 21.1.259, so those servers are currently unjoinable.

**Suggested fix:** drop the ordinal so the unpacking applies to every return. The `instanceof` check already makes it a no-op for the other returns, and it works on both old and new NeoForge builds:

        original = (PacketCodec<? super PacketByteBuf, ? extends Custom

## API Renamings
In preparation for future unobfuscated versions of the game, owo-lib is now developed using the official Mojang Mappings and relevant API elements have been renamed accordingly. Besides a number of straight-forward adaptations (like `World` -> `Level`), this also meant that **the core class of owo-ui (previously `Component`) had to be renamed to `UIComponent`** to avoid a name collision with `net.minecraft.network.chat.Component`. Related classes follow suit, e.g. `ParentComponent` -> `ParentUIComponent`, `Containers` -> `UIContainers`.

## Language Extensions
In addition to Rich Translations, owo-lib now supports nested language files which help to greatly reduce repetition in language keys. Additionally, to reduce conflict potential, **all of owo's language extensions are now opt-in**. Check out the relevant [section of the docs](https://docs.wispforest.io/owo/data-extensions/nested-lang).

## JSON5 Support
The majority of JSON files in any data/resource pack can be converted to use JSON5 when owo-lib is configured to read and convert them to JSON on-the-fly. Once again, check out [the docs](https://docs.wispforest.io/owo/data-extensions/json5).

title: NeoForge docs: Access Transformers
text:
# Access Transformers

Access Transformers (ATs for short) allow for widening the visibility and modifying the `final` flags of classes, methods, and fields. They allow modders to access and modify otherwise inaccessible members in classes outside their control.

The [specification document][specs] can be viewed on the NeoForged GitHub.

## Adding ATs

Adding an Access Transformer to your mod project is as simple as adding a single line into your `build.gradle`:

Access Transformers need to be declared in `build.gradle`. AT files can be specified anywhere as long as they are copied to the `resources` output directory on compilation.

```groovy
// In build.gradle:
// This block is where your mappings version is also specified
minecraft {
    accessTransformers {
        file('src/main/resources/META-INF/accesstransformer.cfg')
    }
}
```

By default, NeoForge will search for `META-INF/accesstransformer.cfg`. If the `build.gradle` specifies access transformers in any other location, then their location needs to be defined within `neoforge.mods.toml`:

```toml
# In neoforge.mods.toml:
[[accessTransformers]]
## The file is relative to the output directory of the resources, or the root path inside the jar when compiled
## The 'resources' directory represents the root output directory of the resources
file="META-INF/accesstransformer.cfg"
```

Additionally, multiple AT files can be specified and will be applied in order. This can be useful for larger mods with multiple packages.

```

// In build.gradle:
minecraft {
    accessTransformers {
        file('src/main/resources/accesstransformer_main.cfg')
        file('src/additions/resources/accesstransformer_additions.cfg')
    }
}
```

```toml
# In neoforge.mods.toml
[[accessTransformers]]
file="accesstransformer_main.cfg"

[[accessTransformers]]
file="accesstransformer_additions.cfg"
```

After adding or modifying any Access Transformer, the Gradle project must be refreshed for the transformations to take effect.

## The Access Transformer Specification

### Comments

All text after a `#` until the end of the line will be treated as a comment and will not be parsed.

### Access Modifiers

Access modifiers specify to what new member visibility the given target will be transformed to. In decreasing order of visibility:

- `public` - visible to all classes inside and outside its package
- `protected` - visible only to classes inside the package and subclasses
- `default` - visible only to classes inside the package
- `private` - visible only to inside the class

A special modifier `+f` and `-f` can be appended to the aforementioned modifiers to either add or remove respectively the `final` modifier, which prevents subclassing, method overriding, or field modification when applied.

:::danger
Directives only modify the method they directly reference; any over

title: NeoForge docs: Access Transformers
text:
modifiers to either add or remove respectively the `final` modifier, which prevents subclassing, method overriding, or field modification when applied.

:::danger
Directives only modify the method they directly reference; any overriding methods will not be access-transformed. It is advised to ensure transformed methods do not have non-transformed overrides that restrict the visibility, which will result in the JVM throwing an error.

Examples of methods that can be safely transformed are `final` methods (or methods in `final` classes), and `static` methods. `private` methods are generally safe as well; however, they could cause unintentional overrides in any subtypes, so some additional manual validation should be performed.
:::

### Targets and Directives

#### Classes

To target classes:

```
<access modifier> <fully qualified class name>
```

Inner classes are denoted by combining the fully qualified name of the outer class and the name of the inner class with a `$` as separator.

#### Fields

To target fields:

```
<access modifier> <fully qualified class name> <field name>
```

#### Methods

Targeting methods require a special syntax to denote the method parameters and return type:

```
<access modifier> <fully qualified class name> <method name>(<parameter types>)<return type>
```

##### Specifying Types

Also called "descriptors": see the [Java Virtual Machine Specification, SE 21, sections 4.3.2 and 4.3.3][jvmdescriptors] for more technical details.

- `B` - `byte`, a signed byte
- `C` - `char`, a Unicode character code point in UTF-16
- `D` - `double`,

- `B` - `byte`, a signed byte
- `C` - `char`, a Unicode character code point in UTF-16
- `D` - `double`, a double-precision floating-point value
- `F` - `float`, a single-precision floating-point value
- `I` - `integer`, a 32-bit integer
- `J` - `long`, a 64-bit integer
- `S` - `short`, a signed short
- `Z` - `boolean`, a `true` or `false` value
- `[` - references one dimension of an array
    - Example: `[[S` refers to `short[][]`
- `L<class name>;` - references a reference type
    - Example: `Ljava/lang/String;` refers to `java.lang.String` reference type _(note the use of slashes instead of periods)_
- `(` - references a method descriptor, parameters should be supplied here or nothing if no parameters are present
    - Example: `<method>(I)Z` refers to a method that requires an integer argument and returns a boolean
- `V` - indicates a method returns no value, can only be used at the end of a method descriptor
    - Example: `<method>()V` refers to a method that has no arguments and returns nothing

title: NeoForge docs: Extensible Enums
text:
# Extensible Enums

Extensible Enums are an enhancement of specific Vanilla enums to allow new entries to be added. This is done by modifying the compiled bytecode of the enum at runtime to add the elements.

## `IExtensibleEnum`

All enums that can have new entries implement the `IExtensibleEnum` interface. This interface acts as a marker to allow the `RuntimeEnumExtender` launch plugin service to know what enums should be transformed.

:::warning
You should **not** be implementing this interface on your own enums. Use maps or registries instead depending on your usecase.  
Enums which are not patched to implement the interface cannot have the interface added to them via mixins or coremods due to the order the transformers run in.
:::

### Creating an Enum Entry

To create new enum entries, a JSON file needs to be created and referenced in the `neoforge.mods.toml` with the `enumExtensions` entry of a `[[mods]]` block. The specified path must be relative to the `resources` directory:
```toml
# In neoforge.mods.toml:
[[mods]]
## The file is relative to the output directory of the resources, or the root path inside the jar when compiled
## The 'resources' directory represents the root output directory of the resources
enumExtensions="META-INF/enumextensions.json"
```

The definition of the entry consists of the target enum's class name, the new field's name (must be prefixed with the mod ID), the descriptor of the constructor to use for constructing the

title: NeoForge docs: Extensible Enums
NeoForge docs: Extensible Enums
NeoForge docs: Extensible Enums
text:
must only contain the parameters visible in the source code, omitting the hidden constant name and ordinal parameters.  
If a constructor is marked with the `@ReservedConstructor` annotation, then it cannot be used for modded enum constants.

#### Parameters

The parameters can be specified in three ways with limitations depending on the parameter types:

- Inline in the JSON file as an array of constants (only allowed for primitive values, Strings and for passing null to any reference type)
- As a reference to a field of type `EnumProxy<TheEnum>` in a class from the mod (see `EnumProxy` example above)
    - The first parameter specifies the target enum and the subsequent parameters are the ones to be passed to the enum constructor
- As a reference to a method returning `Object`, where the return value is the parameter value to use. The method must have exactly two parameters of type `int` (index of the parameter) and `Class<?>` (expected type of the parameter)
    - The `Class<?>` object should be used to cast (`Class#cast()`) the return value in order to keep `ClassCastException`s in mod code.

:::warning
The fields and/or methods used as sources for parameter values should be in a separate class to avoid unintentionally loading mod classes too early.
:::

Certain parameters have additional rules:

- If the parameter is an int ID parameter related to a `@IndexedEnum` annotation on the enum, then it is ignored and replaced by the entry's ordinal. If said parameter is specified inline in the JSON, then it must be specified as `-1`, otherwise an

title: NeoForge docs: Extensible Enums
text:

- If the parameter is a String name parameter related to a `@NamedEnum` annotation on the enum, then it must be prefixed by the mod ID in the `namespace:path` format known from `ResourceLocation`s, otherwise an exception is thrown.

#### Retrieving the Generated Constant

The generated enum constant can be retrieved via `TheEnum.valueOf(String)`. If a field reference is used to provide the parameters, then the constant can also be retrieved from the `EnumProxy` object via `EnumProxy#getValue()`.

## Contributing to NeoForge

To add a new extensible enum to NeoForge, there are at least two required things to do:

- Make the enum implement `IExtensibleEnum` to mark that this enum should be transformed via the `RuntimeEnumExtender`.
- Add a `getExtensionInfo` method that returns `ExtensionInfo.nonExtended(TheEnum.class)`.

Further action is required depending on specific details about the enum:

- If the enum has an int ID parameter which should match the entry's ordinal, then the enum should be annotated with `@NumberedEnum` with the ID's parameter index as the annotation's value if it's not the first parameter
- If the enum has a String name parameter which is used for serialization and should therefore be namespaced, then the enum should

Finally, the `flags` parameter is an update mask, as used in [`Level#setBlock`][setblock].

### Using a Custom Packet

By using a dedicated update packet, you can send packets yourself whenever you need to. This is the most versatile, but also the most complex variant, as it requires setting up a network handler. You can send a packet to all players tracking the block entity by using `PacketDistrubtor#sendToPlayersTrackingChunk`. Please see the [Networking][networking] section for more information.

:::caution
It is important that you do safety checks, as the `BlockEntity` might already be destroyed/replaced when the message arrives at the player. You should also check if the chunk is loaded via `Level#hasChunkAt`.
:::

text:
# Blocks

Blocks are essential to the Minecraft world. They make up all the terrain, structures, and machines. Chances are if you are interested in making a mod, then you will want to add some blocks. This page will guide you through the creation of blocks, and some of the things you can do with them.

## One Block to Rule Them All

Before we get started, it is important to understand that there is only ever one of each block in the game. A world consists of thousands of references to that one block in different locations. In other words, the same block is just displayed a lot of times.

Due to this, a block should only ever be instantiated once, and that is during [registration]. Once the block is registered, you can then use the registered reference as needed.

Unlike most other registries, blocks can use a specialized version of `DeferredRegister`, called `DeferredRegister.Blocks`. `DeferredRegister.Blocks` acts basically like a `DeferredRegister<Block>`, but with some minor differences:

- They are created via `DeferredRegister.createBlocks("yourmodid")` instead of the regular `DeferredRegister.create(...)` method.
- `#register` returns a `DeferredBlock<T extends Block>`, which extends `DeferredHolder<Block, T>`. `T` is the type of the class of the block we are registering.
- There are a few helper methods for registering block. See [below] for more details.

So now, let's register our blocks:

```java
//BLOCKS is a DeferredRegister.Blocks
public static final DeferredBlock<Block>

title: NeoForge docs: Blocks
text:
block. See [below] for more details.

So now, let's register our blocks:

```java
//BLOCKS is a DeferredRegister.Blocks
public static final DeferredBlock<Block> MY_BLOCK = BLOCKS.register("my_block", () -> new Block(...));
```

After registering the block, all references to the new `my_block` should use this constant. For example, if you want to check if the block at a given position is `my_block`, the code for that would look something like this:

```java
level.getBlockState(position) // returns the blockstate placed in the given level (world) at the given position
        //highlight-next-line
        .is(MyBlockRegistrationClass.MY_BLOCK);
```

This approach also has the convenient effect that `block1 == block2` works and can be used instead of Java's `equals` method (using `equals` still works, of course, but is pointless since it compares by reference anyway).

:::danger
Do not call `new Block()` outside registration! As soon as you do that, things can and will break:

- Blocks must be created while registries are unfrozen. NeoForge unfreezes registries for you and freezes them later, so registration is your time window to create blocks.
- If you try to create and/or register a block when registries are frozen again, the game will crash and report a `null` block, which can be very confusing.
- If you still manage to have a dangling block instance, the game will not recognize it while syncing and saving, and replace it with air.
:::

## Creating Blocks

As discussed before, we
